map.：基准时间 = 厚度(mm) × 10（分钟）；温度系数 = 1 + |温度 −: Base time = thickness (mm) × 10 (minutes); temperature coefficient = 1 + |temperature − 38.5| × 0.05; activity coefficient = 5000 ÷ enzyme activity; bating time = base time × temperature coefficient × activity coefficient. The optimum temperature is 37-40°C; below 30°C the enzyme is not active enough and the bath should be warmed, and above 45°C the enzyme denatures easily so it should be cooled.

If the temperature drops to 30°C, the temperature coefficient is 1+|30−38.5|×0.05 = 1.425, giving 28.5 min; if activity falls to 2500, the activity coefficient becomes 2, doubling the time to 40 min.
map.温度偏低为什么要延长时间？: Why must the time be extended at low temperature?
map.酶催化速率随温度下降而降低，为达到同等软化程度需延长作用时间；但更稳妥的做法是先: The catalytic rate falls with temperature, so more contact time is needed to reach the same degree of bating. The safer approach is to warm to 37-40°C before adding the enzyme, avoiding fibre damage from a long soak.
map.软化过度有什么后果？: What are the consequences of over-bating?
map.过度软化会水解皮纤维导致松面、强度下降甚至烂面；软化是不可逆过程，须密切观察、及: Over-bating hydrolyses the collagen fibres, causing grain slackening, loss of strength and even a rotten surface. Bating is irreversible, so watch closely and stop in time, adding the enzyme in batches when necessary.
